claims.text: The starting material is a nanoscale coating of alternating FCC and BCC high-entropy-alloy layers with thicknesses in the tens of nanometers.
The FCC/BCC interfaces are coherent and possess pronounced chemical short-range order.
Chemical short-range order develops preferentially at coherent FCC/BCC interfaces.
Interfacial short-range order alters local lattice parameters and stacking-fault energies.
Interfacial short-range order locally increases stacking-fault energy.
The increased local stacking-fault energy raises the barriers to dislocation nucleation and cross-layer transmission.
Impeded cross-layer dislocation transmission produces dislocation pile-ups along the interfaces.
The interfacial barrier makes progressive deformation under sustained load proceed through a slow, interface-mediated creep mechanism.
Progressive deformation involves diffusion-assisted interfacial sliding.
Reducing short-range order reduces interfacial coherency and facilitates dislocation transfer across layers.
Reducing interfacial short-range order will increase the creep rate relative to the SRO-rich baseline.
Reducing interfacial short-range order will produce more homogeneous plastic flow and less localized dislocation pile-up.
Sustained loading of the SRO-rich baseline will increase dislocation density and localize strain at multilayer interfaces.
The SRO-rich as-deposited baseline exhibits a moderate creep rate and localized interfacial dislocation pile-up.
Temperatures of approximately 500–700 °C permit plastic deformation in high-entropy alloys while appreciable mechanical strength remains.
At the proposed temperatures, diffusion remains limited and complete thermal recovery, recrystallization, and phase instability are avoided.

Rapid quenching with minimal post-deposition thermal treatment promotes interfacial short-range order, whereas an additional anneal can disorder it without significantly changing the rest of the microstructure.
The relative contributions of short-range order and geometric confinement to creep have not been established.
The strength–creep-tolerance trade-off may change with minor compositional modifications.

Failure of reduced-SRO specimens to show either a statistically significant creep-rate increase or reduced pile-up localization relative to the SRO-rich control would falsify the proposed SRO-mediated barrier mechanism.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify constant low-to-moderate stress rates, whereas the falsification experiment specifies constant load. A constant stress rate and a constant load are distinct loading protocols.
